identity_notes: The label identity covers multiple distinct pumpkin plant parts and preparations (whole seed, seed kernel, seed oil, seed extract, ointment/oleogel), per the coordinator's note to record plant part and preparation exactly as stated -- this was done in intervention_as_stated for every kept record. Two clearly separated evidence clusters dominate: (1) BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA / lower urinary tract symptoms, with the largest and best trial being the GRANU study (25196580, n=1,431) which found pumpkin seed's superiority over placebo was only descriptive, not statistically confirmed on its pre-specified primary criterion -- despite this, expert consensus/guideline-style pieces (31852006, 38411727) still credit pumpkin seed favorably; other BPH trials mostly compare pumpkin seed oil against active drug comparators (tamsulosin, prazosin, saw palmetto) rather than placebo, and are consistently non-inferior-to-inferior versus the drug, not clearly superior. (2) HAIR LOSS / ANDROGENETIC ALOPECIA, where a single well-designed RCT (24864154) found pumpkin seed oil significantly increased hair count vs. placebo, reinforced by inclusion in a recent network meta-analysis (41561175) with its own effect estimate -- this is probably the single strongest, cleanest positive signal for this identity. Retrieved literature is heavily contaminated by (a) pure plant-agronomy/agricultural-science studies of pumpkin cultivation (irrigation, salinity, fertilizer, heavy metals, nanoparticles, transcriptomics) with zero human relevance, and (b) false keyword matches where 'Pumpkin' is a trial nickname or medical device name unrelated to the plant (an insulin-pump-therapy trial for pediatric diabetes, and 'Pumpkin' as a specific pediatric ventricular-assist-device brand) -- both categories were rejected as off_topic. A safety signal cluster of pumpkin-seed bezoar/rectal-impaction case reports (from excessive whole-seed consumption) and one cucurbitacin food-poisoning case (from bitter/wild-type squash, not a standard supplement) was routed to handoff.
